title: Modelling the load: virtual users, think time and ramp-up

videos.script: A test plan says: one hundred users. It sounds like a load. It is not one yet. {{plan}} A hundred people who read each page for four seconds ask for about twenty-five pages a second. A hundred programs that never pause ask for as much as the server can answer. {{two}} Same number of users. Completely different loads. {{same}} This lesson is about the missing half of that sentence. How people arrive, how long they think, and how fast the test lets them in. {{model}} You will see the two models side by side. Users who wait for an answer, and arrivals that do not. {{models}} Then one small law ties it together. The number inside equals the rate in, times the time spent inside. {{law}} With it, the box office's ten o'clock sale stops being a story. Twelve hundred people in a minute becomes a hundred requests a second, and two hundred and forty virtual users for the show page. {{sale}} And then you measure it, to see whether the arithmetic was right. {{measure}}
